outcomes: A TypeScript service pushes its metrics, spans and log records to the OTLP/HTTP collector its environment, its telemetry plugin or its log sink names, with the same resource and authenticated for that collector, and sends nothing when none names one
An unreachable or failing collector degrades observability and never fails a request, a log call or a shutdown
Metric series stay bounded whatever paths callers request
Every instance of a scaled-out service writes its own metric series, so the collector accepts what each instance pushes
A span a TypeScript service records joins the caller's trace
An operator tightens or caps the traces and logs of every service from its OTLP endpoint, without a redeploy, and an overloaded endpoint slows its senders down
nonGoals: Defining the OTLP/JSON envelope, its signal paths, its resource keys or its golden bytes, which telemetry/otlp-push-contract owns
Running a collector, or defining collector-side retention, sampling or routing
A /metrics scrape endpoint or an OpenTelemetry exporter SDK dependency
Minting a credential: a runtime package registers the token source for its platform

text: An explicit telemetry() plugin is off by default and when disabled, and enabling it without an endpoint leaves it inert, so no collector is installed and nothing leaves the process.
Enabling it with an endpoint installs a collector at warmup that records every HTTP request without further wiring.
An application whose environment sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT records every HTTP request and pushes its metrics and spans to that collector, with no telemetry() plugin in its composition.
Without that endpoint, or with OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true, the application installs no collector and sends nothing.
An application that installs telemetry() keeps that plugin's configuration, and the environment adds no second collector, so a request is counted once.

An application whose environment sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, without OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true, attaches an OTLP log sink to its root logger when it starts, so its records reach <endpoint>/v1/logs with no sink in its code.
A root logger that already holds an OTLP log sink keeps it, and the environment attaches no second one.
Applications in one process share that sink: the last to stop, or to fail its start, detaches and closes it, flushing its records; a run() runner flushes it when it returns.

The resource of every metrics, traces and logs request names the service from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, then the service.name pair of OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, then the plugin's app option or the log sink's serviceName option, then unknown.
Every other key=value pair of OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES reaches the resource of every metrics, traces and logs request; putnami.framework keeps the value the framework sets.
Every metrics, traces and logs request carries a service.instance.id unique to the process, so two processes started from one environment push distinct series.
A service.instance.id that OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES sets is kept.
The telemetry middleware runs before every other middleware of every HTTP server the application composes, in a sub-module too, so a request an inner middleware refuses is still counted and traced.
Telemetry starts no HTTP server of its own: an application without one keeps its collector for custom metrics and listens on no port.
Each push of metrics, spans or log records asks the token source registered for the collector endpoint for its bearer, and a static bearer wins over the source.
When the source fails, the batch is dropped and nothing is sent without a credential.
The first collector refusal (401 or 403) and the first credential failure each log one warning per plugin or log sink; later ones stay silent and no failure reaches the application.

The collector buckets every measurement by Unix second: a counter sums its increments, a gauge keeps its last value, and a histogram keeps count, sum, min, max and its count in each bucket of the bounds telemetry/otlp-push-contract sets for http.server.duration.
Attributed counters and histograms aggregate by name and attribute set.
A periodic drain returns only completed seconds, in time order, and the shutdown drain returns every bucket, the current second included.

The HTTP middleware counts each request in http.server.request_count and records its duration in http.server.duration, in ms, labeled http.method, http.route and http.status_code as telemetry/otlp-push-contract defines.

http.route is the route pattern, never the resolved path: an unmatched request takes __unmatched__ and a nonstandard method takes _OTHER, so no request adds a series of its own, and no metric name carries a route or status.
The sender renders drained buckets as one OTLP/JSON metrics request whose resource carries the service name and putnami.framework typescript, under the putnami scope.

A counter becomes a monotonic delta sum with an integer point, a gauge a double point, a histogram a point with its count, sum, min, max, bounds and bucket counts, and a metric seen in several buckets one point per bucket.
A metric the collector describes carries its unit and description.
No buckets render an empty request.
The sender posts metrics to <endpoint>/v1/metrics and spans to <endpoint>/v1/traces, collapsing trailing slashes on the base URL.

It sends the body verbatim with the configured extra headers, adds an Authorization bearer header only when a token is set, and resolves a non-2xx response or a network error as not ok instead of throwing.
The plugin pushes metrics every 60 s and spans at most 30 s apart, or at once when 512 wait; stopping pushes the rest of both.
metricIntervalS and spanBatchDelayS override the defaults, then OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY in ms; OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE sets the batch size.
An environment value other than a positive integer of digits is ignored, and a period beyond a timer's limit is capped.
The defaults equal the protocol's export contract fixture.
The OTLP log sink posts its buffered records as one logs request to <endpoint>/v1/logs on close.
Each record carries its severity, message, logger name and error type.
Its context and a single structured data object flatten into dotted attributes, the data object winning over the context, and arrays, cyclic values and BigInt values serialize as strings.

requirements.text: The log sink posts nothing when its buffer is empty, drops its oldest records once its queue cap is reached, and resolves close even when the collector is unreachable, so a wedged collector never fails the logging path.

text: incCounter, setGauge and observeHistogram record into the active collector and do nothing when none is installed.
Stopping an application clears the process-global collector only when it still points at that application's own, so a second application in the same process keeps its telemetry.

A framework span continues a valid ambient W3C trace context as its child, injects its own traceparent over any existing header along with the caller's tracestate and baggage, and, when sampled, records exactly once with its kind, status and attributes.
A remote context with an all-zero trace ID is refused, and an oversized tracestate or baggage is dropped rather than propagated.

A framework span without a parent samples by the telemetry/otlp-push-contract rule, from the traces option of telemetry() or the protocol defaults, and each telemetry.traces config key overrides its field.
A span with a parent takes the parent's sampled flag whatever the budget.
A span records only when sampled, and injects its flag either way.
Each root decision counts in trace.decisions on the active collector.

While it runs, the plugin reloads the config sources every 30 seconds with readConfig() and applies a changed telemetry.traces value to the next root decision, without a restart; a source that keeps its first load for the process, such as CONFIG_DATA or a Cloud remote source, shows no change.
A value out of range, or a section that fails to load, keeps the settings in force and warns.
The sampler's update() applies settings the same way at runtime, and they hold until the config section itself changes.

Every OTLP push, the log sink included, reads the Putnami-Export-Directive header of each collector response and applies it by the telemetry/otlp-push-contract rule: to the installed trace sampler and to the level of every logger that checks it, until its ttl ends.
trace.decisions and log.records keep counting the roots and records a directive drops.
A 429 response with a Retry-After delays the next push of its own signal only.
